With an open SaaS platform that supports easy consolidation and enrichment of any data, DataVisor's fraud and anti-money laundering (AML) solutions scale infinitely and enable organizations to act on fast-evolving fraud and money laundering activities in real time. Its patented unsupervised machine learning technology, advanced device intelligence, powerful decision engine, and investigation tools work together to provide significant performance lift from day one.  We are looking for a creative, hands-on engineering leader to help expand our streaming and database systems, improve our core detection algorithms, and automate the end-to-end training process.  Own the technical direction of the real-time detection platform, including streaming, storage, and the training pipelines that support it.

 Mentor engineers and raise the bar for system design, code quality, operational excellence, and technical execution.

 Partner directly with Product, TAM, and customer-facing teams on customer-impacting issues, ensuring clear impact assessment, prioritization, ownership, and next steps. 
 Define how the team uses AI agents and AI-assisted tools in engineering workflows, including verification standards and safe usage practices. 
 Build, evaluate, and improve LLM- and agent-assisted tools for engineering and operations use cases, such as triage, root-cause analysis, alert summarization, and evaluation harnesses. 
 8+ years of software development experience. 
 2+ years of technical leadership experience as a tech lead, staff engineer, engineering manager, or similar role. 
 Proven ability to lead technical outcomes across a team, including work you did not personally implement. 
 Deep production experience with Java, along with working proficiency in Python and Shell scripting. 
 Experience designing, building, shipping, and operating distributed real-time systems at scale. 
 Strong knowledge of computer systems, relational databases, and SQL. 
 Experience building and optimizing multithreaded and concurrent applications. 
 Hands-on experience with Cassandra, Yugabyte, Flink, Spark, or Kafka.

 The Operations Data Specialist is part of Woodfibre LNG 's Engineering Support team and is responsible for implementing and maintaining the Engineering Data Warehouse (EDW).  · Lead the implementation, configuration, build-out, and operational deployment of the Engineering Data Warehouse (EDW).

 · Experience working in and managing an Engineering Data Warehouse (or Digital Twin) for a large industrial facility

 What is The Role 
 Elasticsearch powers search, observability, and AI retrieval (RAG) for the world's largest organizations. We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer to lead competitive benchmarking initiatives within the Elasticsearch Performance team. 
 You will develop representative workloads, automate reproducible experiments, and investigate how Elasticsearch compares with alternative systems. Your work will identify performance strengths, gaps, and tradeoffs, guide engineering improvements, and help customers make informed technical decisions.
 This is a hands-on engineering role focused on building benchmarks and investigating performance, with technical publishing as a shared responsibility alongside engineering and content partners.
 A typical investigation might ask how Elasticsearch and an alternative system compare under concurrent ingestion and hybrid search, at comparable retrieval quality and cost, and which engineering changes would improve the outcome. This role offers the opportunity to connect deep performance analysis with product improvements and public technical work.
 What You Will Be Doing 
 Own prioritized competitive benchmarking initiatives across search, vector and hybrid retrieval, and analytical and observability workloads.
 Build and maintain automated benchmark harnesses, datasets, query sets, and load profiles that reflect real-world usage, including concurrent ingestion and querying.
 Design fair comparisons with documented system versions, configurations, tuning decisions, resource budgets, and functional differences.
 Evaluate latency distributions, throughput, resource consumption, and cost efficiency. For retrieval workloads, measure performance at comparable recall or relevance targets.
 Adapt and extend workload-appropriate tools such as Elasticsearch Rally, ClickBench, and vector search benchmark frameworks.
 Investigate performance differences using profiling, system metrics, and controlled experiments; collaborate with engineering teams to identify causes and validate improvements.
 Evaluate relevant self-managed and managed cloud deployments, including serverless offerings, accounting for scaling behavior and service constraints.
 Work with engineering and technical content partners to publish reproducible benchmark artifacts and clear technical reports that explain methodology, findings, limitations, and tradeoffs.

 What You Bring 
 Solid software engineering skills, with experience building maintainable automation and analysis tools in Python or another relevant programming language.
 Hands-on experience evaluating and diagnosing performance in distributed systems, databases, or search infrastructure.
 Depth in at least one relevant area (search, vector retrieval, analytical databases, or observability systems) and the ability to learn unfamiliar systems.
 Experience designing representative datasets and workloads, including query patterns, concurrency, and ingestion behavior.
 Sound experimental judgment, including repeated measurements, variability analysis, warm-up and cache effects, and the distinction between meaningful changes and measurement noise.

 Clear technical writing and communication skills, with the ability to explain complex findings and their limitations.
 Solid collaboration skills and the ability to turn performance evidence into applicable engineering recommendations.

Project 
 The Woodfibre LNG Project is located approximately 7 km west-southwest of Squamish, British Columbia. It involves the construction and operation of a liquefied natural gas export facility on the previous Woodfibre pulp mill site. The facility will have LNG storage capacity of approximately 250,000 m³ and production capacity of approximately 2.1 million tonnes per year.
 Woodfibre Management Ltd. is a privately held Canadian company based in Vancouver and a subsidiary of Pacific Energy Corporation Limited.
 Position 
 The Senior HSS Specialist, Commissioning and Start Up is a senior role supporting Woodfibre LNG ’s Health, Safety and
 Security function during late construction, commissioning readiness, commissioning and start-up.
 The role will provide senior technical HSS support for development and delivery of commissioning and start-up deliverables, including procedures, work packages, readiness and assurance tools, and field implementation support. The successful candidate will help ensure HSS requirements are practical, aligned with Woodfibre expectations, and ready for implementation at site.
 The incumbent will work closely with the Director, Health, Safety & Security, the Site HSS Lead / HSS Manager, Operations, commissioning, operations, construction, EPC and contractor teams to ensure safe commissioning and start-up of the Woodfibre LNG Facility.
 Key Responsibilities 
 The successful applicant will support in the following areas:
 • Commissioning and Start-Up Readiness
 • Provide HSS oversight and field guidance for commissioning and start-up readiness.
 • Define, prioritize, and steward commissioning HSS deliverables.
 • Review and guide commissioning HSS procedures, plans, work packs, assurance tools, and readiness evidence.
 • Support integration of HSS requirements into commissioning execution planning.
 • Provide HSS input into commissioning risk assessments, SIMOPS planning, permit to work interfaces, isolation and LOTO interfaces, pre-start-up safety review processes, and readiness reviews.
 • Help verify that HSS controls are understood, implemented, and effective before higher-risk commissioning and start-up activities proceed.
 • Support field implementation of commissioning HSS requirements through coaching, verification, and intervention where required.
 • Identify schedule, resource, quality, competency, and execution risks that could affect HSS readiness for commissioning, start-up, or operations.
 Operations HSS Management System
 • Support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Operations HSS Management System.
 • Help integrate Operations HSS requirements into the Woodfibre Management System.
 • Support Safety and Loss Management System readiness by ensuring HSS requirements are aligned, practical, and field-usable.
 • Lead development and implementation of assigned Operations HSS procedures, standards, tools, and field practices.
 • Ensure Operations HSS requirements are fit for purpose, scalable, and practical for a compact, remote LNG facility.
 • Support the transition from construction-phase HSS arrangements to Operations HSS requirements.
 • Help define the Operations HSS operating rhythm, including inspections, field verifications, action tracking, leadership reviews, and performance reporting.
 • Ensure systems and tools support effective decisions rather than adding unnecessary complexity.
 • Support development of Operations HSS training requirements and field implementation plans.
 • Ensure HSS expectations are clearly understood by Operations personnel, contractors, and site leaders.
 Field Assurance and Contractor Oversight
 • Help ensure Operations and site teams conduct inspections, control verifications, field checks, and corrective action follow-up.
 • Monitor and verify contractor implementation of applicable HSS requirements.
 • Conduct and support field inspections, audits, observations, and control verifications.
 • Assess the effectiveness of corrective actions and confirm closure evidence where required.
 • Support incident reporting, investigation, learning, and corrective action management.
 • Review incident investigation outputs for quality, completeness, and practical corrective actions.
 • Use assurance results, field observations, incident data, and performance metrics to identify trends, weak controls, and improvement opportunities.
 • Support reporting of HSS performance, key risks, assurance findings, and priority actions.
 Security and Emergency Management Interfaces
 • Work closely with the Corporate Security Manager to support field implementation of approved security strategies, plans, and controls.
 • Support site-level coordination where security requirements affect HSS execution, contractor management, access control, workforce behaviour, or field readiness.
 • Work closely with the Emergency Response Manager to support field implementation of emergency response strategies, plans, drills, exercises, and readiness requirements.
 • Support emergency response and security readiness as part of integrated site execution.
 • Occupational health and safety certification, applicable university degree, technical diploma, or equivalent combination of education and experience.
 • Minimum 10 years of HSS experience in oil and gas, LNG, petrochemical, chemical, marine terminal, heavy industrial, or major project environments.
 • Experience supporting commissioning, start-up, operations readiness, or operations in a major industrial setting.
 • Experience developing or implementing HSS procedures, plans, work packages, assurance tools, or field execution requirements for commissioning, start-up, or high-risk industrial work.
 • Strong working knowledge of Canadian occupational health and safety legislation and industrial HSS management systems. British Columbia experience would be an asset.
 • Experience working with EPC contractors, multidisciplinary teams, and contractor workforces.
 • Experience with critical risk management, SIMOPS, permit to work, isolation and LOTO interfaces, job hazard analysis, field assurance, incident investigation, corrective action management, and HSS performance reporting.
 • Experience providing field guidance, coaching, challenge, and practical HSS support to operations, construction, commissioning, and contractor teams.
 Additional Requirements
 • Strong field presence and practical judgment.
 • Able to work independently and provide senior HSS support with limited day-to-day direction.
 • Able to influence, coach, challenge, and escalate issues appropriately.
 • Able to work effectively with Operations, Construction, Commissioning, EPC, contractor, corporate, and functional teams.
 • Able to simplify complex requirements into practical field expectations.
 • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
 • Comfortable working under pressure and managing competing priorities.
 • Proficient with Microsoft Office and HSS management systems or reporting tools.
 • Able to meet the physical demands of a site-based industrial role.
 • Must comply with company substance abuse policy requirements, including pre-access testing.
 • Must have authorization to work in Canada. 
 Only qualified candidates legally entitled to work in Canada will be contacted.

Sadie is building technology for hospitality.
 We're looking for an account executive to win new restaurant customers in Vancouver or Calgary, and to run every deal yourself from the first lead to the signed agreement.
 This is a field role. You'll find restaurants through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits, then meet owners in person and show them Sadie working on their own calls. You'll work with onboarding and customer success, so that what you sell goes live well. You'll carry monthly and quarterly targets and own the forecast behind them.
 You decide where to spend your time and which deals to pursue, within agreed pricing and terms. AI should be part of how you work. Use it to research restaurants before a visit, prepare demos, draft proposals and follow-ups, and plan your territory. You're responsible for the quality of everything that goes out under your name.
 What we value
 Sound judgement about which deals are real.
 Taking responsibility for your number and finishing work without being chased.
 Understanding how a restaurant makes money, and caring whether Sadie improves it.
 Curiosity about why a deal was lost, and a willingness to change your approach.
 The honesty to say a deal is slipping before the forecast says it for you.
 What you'll do
 Win new restaurants, from first visit to signed agreement 
 Most of your time goes on live deals, and most of those deals happen in person. You'll sit down with owners and general managers in their restaurants to learn how the phone is handled today: who answers it, what gets missed during service, and what those missed calls cost in bookings and orders. Then you'll demo Sadie against that picture.
 You'll scope what the restaurant needs, write the proposal, negotiate terms and get the agreement signed. 
 Most of the judgement is in qualification. A good demo with someone who can't sign, or a restaurant Sadie can't serve yet, costs you weeks. You're expected to spot that early and move on.
 Build your own pipeline across your territory 
 You'll generate your own leads through outbound outreach, networking and on-site visits. That means planning which neighbourhoods and restaurant groups to work, walking in at the right time of day, and following up until you get a meeting.
 Hit your targets with a forecast you can defend 
 You're measured against monthly and quarterly sales targets, and the expectation is that you hit them consistently. You'll keep every opportunity accurate in HubSpot, so that stage, value and close date mean something to the people who plan around them.
 Represent Sadie where restaurant people meet 
 You'll attend local industry events, restaurant meetups and trade shows across your geography. You'll decide which ones are worth the evening, run the conversations there, and turn them into meetings within the week.
 For a lot of operators, you'll be the first person from Sadie they meet. What they hear from you is what they'll repeat to other owners.
 Hand over accounts that go live well 
 The restaurant buys Sadie, but the guest ringing to book a table decides whether it works. You'll give onboarding and customer success a written record of what you promised, what the owner expects, and what could go wrong.
 If you oversell, the owner finds out on a Friday night and the guest pays for it. Set expectations you can stand behind.
 What you'll bring
 At least 2 years in a closing sales role, selling software or services to businesses in hospitality (ideally full service restaurants) or experience working at full service restaurants.
 A record of meeting targets, and the ability to explain how you did it.
 Experience running the whole cycle yourself, from prospecting through to signature.
 Comfort with in-person selling, including cold visits and demos in front of a busy owner.
 Strong discovery skills. You can find out what an operator needs in fifteen minutes between services.
 Clear written communication. Your proposals and follow-ups are accurate and short.
 An honest forecast. You'd rather call a deal lost than carry it for another month.
 You use AI every day for research, preparation and drafting, and you check what it produces.
 You organise your own week across a territory and follow through without being managed.
 Useful experience
 Selling to restaurants or other hospitality operators.
 Working in a restaurant yourself, front of house or in management.
 Selling reservations, POS, telephony or other restaurant technology.
 An existing network among restaurant owners in your territory.
 Selling AI products to non-technical buyers.
 Being an early sales hire at a startup.
 Who will enjoy this role
 You like finding out how a business really works. When an owner says they miss calls at seven on a Saturday, you want to know how many, what those calls were for, and what happened to the guest who hung up.
 In a single week you might walk into six restaurants before lunch service, run a demo at a bar between shifts, spend an evening at a trade show, and sit with onboarding to sort out an account you signed. Your schedule follows the restaurant day, and some of your best conversations will happen at three in the afternoon or late at night.
 The hard parts are specific. Owners are busy and sceptical, and many will turn you away mid-service. You'll hear no far more often than yes, and you'll still need to be back through the next door the same afternoon. Some of the material you'd expect to have, such as local case studies or a settled playbook, may not exist yet, and you'll help build it while carrying a number.
 Why this role matters
 Sadie is building technology for hospitality. Restaurants lose revenue to calls nobody picks up, and our product exists to answer them.
 This role is how Sadie reaches the restaurants in your geography. You decide who to visit and how each customer starts. The agreements you sign affect revenue, what onboarding and customer success inherit, and what a guest hears when they ring to book a table.
 You'll own new restaurant business across your territory, with the authority to decide how Sadie wins it.

Raise the technical bar

Every team that processes transactions, for both booking and post-booking, depends on the subledger, so you will shape Hopper's financial platform architecture alongside Finance, Accounting, Payments, and the product engineering teams that rely on it. You will be the primary technical owner of a system where accuracy and full traceability matter most, balancing accounting rigor with the engineering judgment needed to keep it evolving.

 - Own and manage the subledger platform with an outcomes-based mindset, serving as the primary point of contact for technical, accounting, and operational topics related to transaction recording and reconciliation

 - Lead, grow, and mentor a team of engineers, setting technical direction and championing correctness in a system where every entry must balance

 - Drive the architecture of the subledger, evolving the current design toward simplicity and scalability through sound abstractions and automation

 - Ensure all money movements across booking and post-booking flows are accurately accounted for, with full traceability from source event to financial report

 - Build strong, senior-level relationships with Finance and Accounting, translating accounting requirements into system design and surfacing technical constraints early

 - Partner with the Payments, Bookings, Post-Booking, and Data teams that integrate with the subledger, aligning on contracts, data models, and migration paths

 Monthly progress draws and budget reconciliation in Procore. You draft it, your PD reviews it before it finalizes.

 Ludia est une entreprise innovante et dynamique, spécialisée dans le développement de jeux mobiles. Fondée en 2007, nous avons construit une solide réputation en créant des expériences de jeu captivantes et diversifiées, comme Jurassic World the Game, Jurassic World Alive et Dragons: Rise of Berk. 
 Après plusieurs années de collaboration au sein d'un grand groupe, Ludia a retrouvé son indépendance et redevient un acteur québécois, prêt à relever de nouveaux défis! Notre équipe, forte de son expérience, est plus déterminée que jamais à innover, à explorer de nouveaux horizons et à continuer d'offrir des expériences exceptionnelles à nos joueurs à travers le monde. 
 Ludia est à un tournant excitant de son histoire, et nous recherchons des talents passionnés et ambitieux pour nous accompagner dans cette nouvelle aventure. 
 CANDIDATURE SPONTANÉE 
 Chez Ludia, nous sommes toujours à la recherche de personnes créatives, curieuses et passionnées qui souhaitent façonner l’avenir du jeu mobile. 
 Si aucun poste ouvert ne correspond à votre profil pour le moment, pas de souci — nous voulons tout de même faire votre connaissance! 
 En soumettant une candidature spontanée, vous indiquez à notre équipe Talent Acquisition que vous êtes intéressé·e à rejoindre Ludia. Nous ajouterons votre profil à notre vivier de talents et vous contacterons lorsqu’un poste correspondant à votre parcours et à vos aspirations sera disponible.

 Un·e joueur·se d’équipe passionné·e par l’univers du jeu et de l’innovation 
 Une personne ayant de l’expérience ou de l’intérêt pour des domaines comme le game design, la production, l’art, l’animation, l’ingénierie, la data, le QA ou les fonctions de support 
 Ouvert·e à collaborer dans un environnement hybride à Montréal, QC (ou ayant les autorisations nécessaires pour travailler au Canada) 
 Pourquoi nous rejoindre ? 
 Chez Ludia, nous croyons qu'il est essentiel de créer un environnement de travail aussi inspirant que les jeux que nous produisons. Voici ce à quoi vous pouvez vous attendre : 
 💼 Flexibilité  : Horaires flexibles pour promouvoir un équilibre sain entre vie professionnelle et vie privée, possibilité de travailler à distance pour plus de flexibilité dans la manière et le lieu de travail, et un studio dynamique au centre-ville de Montréal, proche des transports en commun.
